box: short-stick (/game/short-stick/) — WAAPI reveal animation guarded by prefers-reduced-motion, proven both ways
method: Two separate real headless Chrome launches (docs/agents/browser-verification.md's documented mechanism, not Emulation.setEmulatedMedia): plain launch on port 9222 (--headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --remote-debugging-port=9222) and a second launch on port 9223 identical except --force-prefers-reduced-motion, each with its own --user-data-dir. Same scripts/driver.mjs script run against both via CDP_PORT=9222 / CDP_PORT=9223, against the same real build served by npx serve dist/ -l 4321. Each run: navigated to /game/short-stick/, wiped storage on-origin, read matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches to confirm the flag actually flipped, started a 4-player round (start-numbered), then repeatedly clicked the next available stick (synchronous click() dispatch, so any node.animate() call in the handler has already run by the time click() returns) and read document.getAnimations() immediately after each click plus 5 samples 50ms apart, at both the passing-screen reveal (renderPassing) and the final result-screen reveal (renderResult). The result screen's DOM text was captured in both runs to prove the outcome is on screen regardless of animation state.
